brief: Large-cap indices sit near record highs but breadth has collapsed: only ~25% of S&P 500 constituents trade above their 50-day average, the lowest such reading ever this close to a record, so participation should stay narrow until yields stabilize, with Tech carrying performance. Industrials rose for the first time in six weeks but remain 8.5% below their August high, pressured by record diesel prices and divided-government odds raising defense-spending uncertainty; Raymond James stays constructive because oil pressure should ease in 2027 and data-center buildout keeps demand for electrical equipment strong. The 10-year yield's fourth straight weekly rise, to 5.17%, came even as oil fell ~4%, implying oil's grip on yields is fading in favor of strong data, Fed hawkishness and technicals; RJ expects yields to moderate as inflation cools. This week's calendar: JOLTS openings holding above 7M, August PCE at 3.7% with core at 3.4%, and ~70k September payrolls. On Iran, RJ's base case is a gradual oil-supply recovery and a $65 12-month WTI forecast, even as the White House rejects Iran's latest proposal.
